headline: Last session: Indian markets extended gains for a third straight week driven by strong foreign fund inflows.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 16 November.

why: Indian benchmark indices extended weekly gains for the third consecutive week supported by FII buying.
Smallcap indices jumped 3.6% and PSU bank stocks surged 7.5% during recent weekly trade.
Lower crude oil prices and foreign fund inflows helped fuel market momentum.
Inflation concerns and global market cues triggered brief pullbacks in benchmark indices during recent sessions.
whatHappening: ONGC took over the disputed Cambay block from Vedanta following a court ruling.
PNB aims to achieve Rs 200 crore quarterly profit from its credit card and cash management verticals starting FY28.
SEBI Chairman Tuhin Pandey announced plans to issue AI usage guidelines for capital markets to safeguard investors.
Motherson is expanding its footprint in India by leveraging global technologies to boost future growth.
summary: Indian equities logged their third straight weekly gain, bolstered by robust FII inflows, lower crude oil prices, and broad-based buying across smallcaps and PSU banks. Meanwhile, regulatory updates and key corporate developments in ONGC, Vedanta, PNB, and Motherson kept individual stocks in focus. Markets remain closed today for the weekend and will resume trading on Monday, 16 November.
